subject: art-design
source_note: Topic structure follows the Eduqas/WJEC GCSE Art and Design specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships.

units.name: Knowledge, Understanding & Skills
units.blurb: The core creative process underpinning all titles

units.name: Component 1: Portfolio
units.blurb: A sustained portfolio of personal work

units.name: Component 2: Externally Set Assignment
units.blurb: Response to a WJEC-set starting point

units.name: Endorsed Titles & Areas of Study
units.blurb: The disciplines a student may specialise in

topics.name: Developing Ideas from Sources
topics.blurb: Drawing on artists, contexts and issues to develop ideas (AO1)

topics.name: Experimenting with Media & Processes
topics.blurb: Refining work through media, materials and techniques (AO2)

topics.name: Recording & Annotation
topics.blurb: Recording observations and judgements visually and in writing (AO3)

topics.name: Portfolio Project
topics.blurb: A sustained portfolio showing the full creative journey

topics.name: ESA Preparatory Work
topics.blurb: Preparatory studies in response to a set starting point

topics.name: ESA Sustained Outcome
topics.blurb: Final outcome produced under sustained focus conditions

topics.name: Fine Art
topics.blurb: Drawing, painting, printmaking, sculpture, mixed and lens-based media

topics.name: Graphic Communication
topics.blurb: Illustration, typography, design for print and interactive design

topics.name: Textile Design
topics.blurb: Constructed, printed, dyed and stitched textiles and fashion

topics.name: Three-Dimensional Design
topics.blurb: Product, architectural, interior and exhibition design, ceramics

topics.name: Photography
topics.blurb: Documentary, studio, location, experimental and moving image

connections.why: Ideas developed from sources are then explored through media and processes
Experimentation is documented through visual recording and annotation
Recorded development leads to resolved personal outcomes
Outcomes must clearly connect back to the ideas and sources that inspired them
The portfolio is built from sustained cycles of the creative process
Skills and approaches honed in the portfolio prepare students for the set assignment
Preparatory studies culminate in the sustained-focus final outcome
Each endorsed title is realised through the same experimentation with media
Photographic imagery frequently feeds graphic communication work
Textile and three-dimensional design overlap in constructed, material-led making
Studying artists and contexts is the starting point for fine-art enquiry
Lens-based experimentation defines the photography title
